subject: Media Literacy
title: Sensationalism and Click Revenue
description: Learn Sensationalism and Click Revenue in one minute.

hook.text: A headline screams 'deadly new virus threat.' The article says the risk is near zero. The headline got the clicks.

buildup.text: Sensationalism exaggerates stories to attract attention. In digital media, clicks directly generate advertising revenue.

discovery.text: The business model creates a perverse incentive: the more alarming or outrageous the headline, the more money it makes.

twist.text: Journalists who write measured, accurate headlines get fewer clicks — and face pressure to sensationalize instead.

climax.text: The economics of attention reward exaggeration and punish nuance. The business model is at war with journalism's mission.

punchline.text: The headline scared you on purpose. Fear clicks. Truth doesn't.

quiz.question: Why does digital media incentivize sensationalism?
options: Clicks generate ad revenue, and alarming headlines get more clicks
